chunks: Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Aban, from Al-Sadusi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever comes to me as a visitor (Za'ir), I will be his intercessor on the Day of Judgment.

key_terms.زَائِراً: Visitor or one who performs Ziyarah

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for performing Ziyarah to the Prophet Muhammad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarah* underscores the unique eschatological privilege of visiting the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.a.w.), linking physical devotion to divine intercession. In Shia tradition, this visitation is not merely commemorative but a means of securing the Prophet’s advocacy on the Day of Judgment, reinforcing the continuity of spiritual connection between the believer and the Ahl al-Bayt. The narration highlights the Prophet’s role as an intercessor, a concept deeply rooted in both Quranic verses and Shia theological understanding of the Hereafter.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 10. Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abān, from Al-Sadūsi, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)), who said:
The Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) said: On the Day of Judgment, I will intercede for those who have come to my Ziyārah.
